summary: A scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Tenzin Dorjee studied under Geshe Lobsang Tsephel, Geshe Sonam Rinchen, and Geshe Dawa. He served as a translator at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and at Pullahari Monastery as General Secretary.

Working in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies, he studied at Sera and Drepung Monasteries, the University of Melbourne, and the University of British Columbia under teachers including Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, and Trulshik Rinpoche.

Specializing in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, he earned a Geshe degree at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics (where he served as president) and studied under Sangye Tenzin Rinpoche and Lopon Tenzin Namdak. He was a Rockefeller Fellow at Rice University (1991).

Ter Ellingson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Concordia College (1966), the University of Chicago (1970), and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1979), and held a post at the University of Washington from 1981 to 2016.

A scholar of history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Sinology, she earned an M.A. from the University of California, Los Angeles. She served at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco, including as Curator of Himalayan Art and Chinese Decorative Art (attested 2001–2003).

Specializing in religious studies and philosophy, he studied at the University of Tokyo (~1923–1926). He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Nihon University, Aichi University, Tohoku University (~1940–1967), and Keio University (~1967–1972).

A scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, she studied at the Universities of Florida, Ceylon, Cornell, Banaras Hindu, Florida State, and Virginia (PhD ~1991). She taught at Virginia, Florida State University (1993), and Indiana University–Purdue University Indianapolis (~1991–2001).

A Buddhist studies scholar, he studied at Ryukoku University (~1925–1931). He held professorships at Taisho University and Gifu Kyoritsu University (~1972), and served as professor emeritus at Ryukoku University (~1972–1982).
Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tetsuhiko Shibata studied at Taisho University under teachers Eijun Hattori, Yukan Ozawa, and Mitsuo Sato.

Active in philosophy and religious studies, he studied at the University of Tokyo (~1877–1880), Heidelberg (~1884–1889), and Leipzig (~1884–1887). He held posts as assistant professor at the University of Tokyo (~1882–1890) and at Toyo University (~1925–1944).

A Buddhist studies scholar, he studied at Waseda University and Komazawa University. He held academic posts at Komazawa University, Peking University, Tomakomai Komazawa University (2006–2007), Tsuru University (2013–2016), and Tohoku Fukushi University (2015–2019).
Tetsuo Suzuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Shizuoka University. He held an assistant professorship at Otani University (attested 1974).

Active in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology, he studied at the University of Tokyo (~1909–1912). He held posts at Toyo, Hosei, Ryukoku, and Otani Universities, Kyoto University (~1925–1934), and the University of Tokyo (~1934–1949), holding the chair in Ethics.
Teun Goudriaan worked in the fields of Indology and religious studies. He held posts at Utrecht University, where he is attested in 1989 and was Professor Emeritus by 2000.
Thanon Chitkament is a scholar in the field of history and archaeology who studied under guide V. D. Gogte and co-guide P. S. Joshi (both attested 2021).

A scholar of Indology and linguistics, he studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1840–1847), where he became Privatdozent in 1850. He was Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Edinburgh (1862) and Professor at the University of Bonn (1875–1889).
An Indologist and linguist, Benfey studied at the University of Göttingen (~1824–1826). He spent his career there as Privatdozent (1834), Lehrmeister (1848), and Ordinarius (1862–1881).
An Indologist and archaeologist, Bloch studied at Leipzig University under Ernst Windisch (~1888–1892) and later studied under Georg Bühler as a Specialschüler (~1892–1895).

An Indologist and linguist, he studied at Königsberg, Bonn, and Paris under Peter von Bohlen, Karl Rosenkranz, Christian Lassen, and Eugène Burnouf. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of London and University College London (~1852–1872).

A linguist and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, he studied at Göttingen (under Theodor Benfey), Vienna, Leiden, and Berlin. He held academic posts at the University of Göttingen (~1861–1864) and the University of Kiel (~1864–1872).
